display_title: 20-1-2 榆树回归：让这种深受喜爱的树重返英国

sentences.en: Mark Rowe investigates attempts to reintroduce elms to Britain
sentences.zh: 马克·罗调查了人们为让榆树重返英国所作的尝试。

sentences.en: Around 25 million elms, accounting for 90% of all elm trees in the UK, died during the 1960s and ’70s of Dutch elm disease.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60至70年代，英国约有2500万棵榆树死于荷兰榆树病，占当时全国榆树总数的90%。

sentences.en: In the aftermath, the elm, once so dominant in the British landscape, was largely forgotten.
sentences.zh: 此后，曾是英国风景中占据主导地位的榆树，在很大程度上被人们淡忘了。

sentences.en: However, there’s now hope the elm may be reintroduced to the countryside of central and southern England.
sentences.zh: 不过，如今人们有望把榆树重新引入英格兰中部和南部的乡村。

sentences.en: Any reintroduction will start from a very low base.
sentences.zh: 重新引种只能从很低的起点开始。

sentences.en: ‘The impact of the disease is difficult to picture if you hadn’t seen what was there before,’ says Matt Elliot of the Woodland Trust.
sentences.zh: 英国林地信托基金会的马特·埃利奥特说：“如果没见过这里从前的样子，就很难想象这场树病造成了多大影响。”

sentences.en: ‘You look at old photographs from the 1960s and it’s only then that you realise the impact [elms had] ... They were significant, large trees ... then they were gone.’
sentences.zh: “看看20世纪60年代的老照片，你这才会明白榆树当年有多重要……那些树高大醒目……后来就这么消失了。”

sentences.en: The disease is caused by a fungus that blocks the elms’ vascular (water, nutrient and food transport) system, causing branches to wilt and die.
sentences.zh: 这种病由一种真菌引起。真菌会堵塞榆树的维管系统，也就是输送水分、养分和食物的系统，导致树枝萎蔫、枯死。

sentences.en: A first epidemic, which occurred in the 1920s, gradually died down, but in the ’70s a second epidemic was triggered by shipments of elm from Canada.
sentences.zh: 20世纪20年代，树病首次大规模流行，后来渐渐平息。但到了70年代，从加拿大运来的榆木又引发了第二次大流行。

sentences.en: The wood came in the form of logs destined for boat building and its intact bark was perfect for the elm bark beetles that spread the deadly fungus.
sentences.zh: 运来的是准备用于造船的原木，树皮完好无损，恰好适合传播这种致命真菌的榆小蠹虫栖身。

sentences.en: This time, the beetles carried a much more virulent strain that destroyed the vast majority of British elms.
sentences.zh: 这一次，小蠹虫携带的菌株致病力强得多，英国绝大多数榆树都因此枯死。

sentences.en: Today, elms still exist in the southern English countryside but mostly only in low hedgerows between fields.
sentences.zh: 如今，英格兰南部乡间仍能看到榆树，但大多只长在田块之间低矮的树篱里。

sentences.en: ‘We have millions of small elms in hedgerows but they get targeted by the beetle as soon as they reach a certain size,’ says Karen Russell, co-author of the report ‘Where we are with elm’.
sentences.zh: 《榆树现状》报告的合著者凯伦·拉塞尔说：“树篱里有数百万棵小榆树，可它们一长到一定大小，就会被小蠹虫盯上。”

sentences.en: Once the trunk of the elm reaches 10–15 centimetres or so in diameter, it becomes a perfect size for beetles to lay eggs and for the fungus to take hold.
sentences.zh: 榆树树干的直径一到十至十五厘米左右，粗细就恰好适合小蠹虫产卵，也适合真菌在树体内生长。

sentences.en: Yet mature specimens have been identified, in counties such as Cambridgeshire, that are hundreds of years old, and have mysteriously escaped the epidemic.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们在剑桥郡等地发现了一些树龄已有数百年的成熟榆树，它们躲过了这场病害，原因不明。

sentences.en: The key, Russell says, is to identify and study those trees that have survived and work out why they stood tall when millions of others succumbed.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔说，关键在于找出并研究那些幸存的榆树，弄清为什么其他数百万棵树纷纷病死，它们却依然挺立。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, opportunities are limited as the number of these mature survivors is relatively small.
sentences.zh: 不过，这样的研究机会有限，因为存活至今的成熟榆树数量相对较少。

sentences.en: ‘What are the reasons for their survival?’ asks Russell.
sentences.zh: “它们为什么能活下来？”拉塞尔问道。

sentences.en: ‘Avoidance, tolerance, resistance?
sentences.zh: “是避开了感染，是能耐受病害，还是有抗病能力？

sentences.en: We don’t know where the balance lies between the three.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道这三个因素各起了多大作用。

sentences.en: I don’t see how it can be entirely down to luck.’
sentences.zh: 我不相信这完全靠运气。”

sentences.en: For centuries, elm ran a close second to oak as the hardwood tree of choice in Britain and was in many instances the most prominent tree in the landscape.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，论英国人选用硬木树种的偏好，榆树紧随橡树之后。在许多地方，它还是风景中最醒目的树。

sentences.en: Not only was elm common in European forests, it became a key component of birch, ash and hazel woodlands.
sentences.zh: 榆树不仅在欧洲森林中很常见，也是桦树、白蜡树和榛树林地中的重要树种。

sentences.en: The use of elm is thought to go back to the Bronze Age, when it was widely used for tools.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，榆木的使用可以追溯到青铜时代，当时它被广泛用来制作工具。

sentences.en: Elm was also the preferred material for shields and early swords.
sentences.zh: 榆木也是制作盾牌和早期刀剑的首选材料。

sentences.en: In the 18th century, it was planted more widely and its wood was used for items such as storage crates and flooring.
sentences.zh: 18世纪，榆树种植得更加广泛，榆木被用来制作储物板条箱、地板等物品。

sentences.en: It was also suitable for items that experienced high levels of impact and was used to build the keel of the 19th-century sailing ship Cutty Sark as well as mining equipment.
sentences.zh: 榆木也适合制作需要承受强烈冲击的物件。19世纪帆船“卡蒂萨克”号的龙骨以及采矿设备就用榆木制成。

sentences.en: Given how ingrained elm is in British culture, it’s unsurprising the tree has many advocates.
sentences.zh: 榆树在英国文化中深深扎了根，这种树拥有众多支持者，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Amongst them is Peter Bourne of the National Elm Collection in Brighton.
sentences.zh: 其中一位便是彼得·伯恩，他来自布赖顿的英国国家榆树收藏机构。

sentences.en: ‘I saw Dutch elm disease unfold as a small boy,’ he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我小时候亲眼见过荷兰榆树病是怎样一步步蔓延的。”

sentences.en: ‘The elm seemed to be part of rural England, but I remember watching trees just lose their leaves and that really stayed with me.’
sentences.zh: “榆树仿佛就是英格兰乡村的一部分。我还记得眼看着那些树的叶子掉光，那一幕一直印在我脑海里。”

sentences.en: Today, the city of Brighton’s elms total about 17,000.
sentences.zh: 如今，布赖顿市约有一万七千棵榆树。

sentences.en: Local factors appear to have contributed to their survival.
sentences.zh: 当地的一些条件似乎帮助这些榆树存活了下来。

sentences.en: Strong winds from the sea make it difficult for the determined elm bark beetle to attack this coastal city’s elm population.
sentences.zh: 海上吹来的强风使顽强的榆小蠹虫很难侵袭这座海滨城市的榆树群。

sentences.en: However, the situation is precarious.
sentences.zh: 不过，眼下的形势并不稳定。

sentences.en: ‘The beetles can just march in if we’re not careful, as the threat is right on our doorstep,’ says Bourne.
sentences.zh: 伯恩说：“我们稍不留神，这些甲虫就会长驱直入，因为威胁就在家门口。”

sentences.en: Any prospect of the elm returning relies heavily on trees being either resistant to, or tolerant of, the disease.
sentences.zh: 榆树能否回归，在很大程度上取决于榆树是否具有抗病性或耐病性。

sentences.en: This means a widespread reintroduction would involve existing or new hybrid strains derived from resistant, generally non-native elm species.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，要大范围重新引种，就得采用现有或新育成的杂交品系。这些品系源自有抗病性的榆树种，而这些树种大多并非本土物种。

sentences.en: A new generation of seedlings have been bred and tested to see if they can withstand the fungus by cutting a small slit on the bark and injecting a tiny amount of the pathogen.
sentences.zh: 研究者已培育出新一代幼苗，并对其进行测试，看它们能否抵御这种真菌。测试时，他们在树皮上划开一个小口，注入微量病原体。

sentences.en: ‘The effects are very quick,’ says Russell.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔说：“很快就能看出结果。”

sentences.en: ‘You return in four to six weeks and trees that are resistant show no symptoms, whereas those that are susceptible show leaf loss and may even have died completely.’
sentences.zh: “四到六周后再来看，抗病的树没有症状，而易感的树已经落叶，有的甚至可能整株都枯死了。”

sentences.en: All of this raises questions of social acceptance, acknowledges Russell.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔承认，这一切都牵涉到公众能否接受的问题。

sentences.en: ‘If we’re putting elm back into the landscape, a small element of it is not native – are we bothered about that?’
sentences.zh: “如果我们把榆树重新引入这片土地，它会带有少量非本土成分。我们介意这一点吗？”

sentences.en: For her, the environmental case for reintroducing elm is strong.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，从环境角度讲，重新引种榆树的理由很充分。

sentences.en: ‘They will host wildlife, which is a good thing.’
sentences.zh: “这些树会为野生生物提供栖息地，这是好事。”

sentences.en: Others are more wary.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则更加谨慎。

sentences.en: ‘On the face of it, it seems like a good idea,’ says Elliot.
sentences.zh: 埃利奥特说：“乍看之下，这似乎是个好主意。”

sentences.en: The problem, he suggests, is that, ‘You’re replacing a native species with a horticultural analogue*.
sentences.zh: 他指出，问题在于：“你用一种园艺培育的近似种替代了本土物种。

sentences.en: You’re effectively cloning.’
sentences.zh: 实际上，你是在克隆。”

sentences.en: There’s also the risk of introducing new diseases.
sentences.zh: 此外，还存在引入新病害的风险。

sentences.en: Rather than plant new elms, the Woodland Trust emphasises providing space to those elms that have survived independently.
sentences.zh: 英国林地信托基金会主张给那些自行存活下来的榆树留出生长空间，而非另栽新树。

sentences.en: ‘Sometimes the best thing you can do is just give nature time to recover ... over time, you might get resistance,’ says Elliot.
sentences.zh: 埃利奥特说：“有时，最好的做法就是给自然一些时间去恢复……时间久了，也许就会出现抗病性。”
